conventions: Comment-only change: add TSDoc comment lines and nothing else; never change, move, reformat or delete a code line, an import, an existing blank line, a release tag, or the copyright header, and add no blank line outside a comment block.

Comment form: a `/**` line, ` * ` text lines, and a ` */` line, indented to the declaration it documents (2 spaces for interface members and class methods, column 0 for top-level functions), as the members of packages/catalog-model/src/entity/Entity.ts are documented.

The first paragraph is one summary sentence ending in a period. When a unit gives remarks, write `@remarks`, then a blank ` *` line, then the remark paragraphs, then a blank ` *` line before the block tags. A blank ` *` line also separates the summary from `@remarks`.

Block tags use `@param name - description` (a hyphen after the name, no trailing period on the description), as packages/catalog-model/src/validation/CommonValidatorFunctions.ts does; `@returns` text follows the same no-trailing-period form.

Wrap comment text at 80 columns including indentation (Prettier does not wrap comments; existing comments in the package wrap near 80). Break only between words and never inside a backtick span or a `{@link ...}` tag.

Any `{`, `}`, `<`, `>` or `@` in prose goes inside backticks, because TSDoc reads them as tags or HTML and API Extractor reports a warning in the API report. Use `{@link X}` only where a unit's rule writes it; every link target is a public export of @backstage/catalog-model.
Write the sentences a unit's rules give, word for word and in that order; do not add, drop or reword a claim. U.S. English. Every statement has been checked against the implementation and its tests.
packages/catalog-model/report.api.md and report-alpha.api.md are regenerated by `yarn build:api-reports` only; no unit edits them.

decisions.topic: Member comments on the eight kind interfaces
decisions.choice: A multi-line `/** ... */` block directly above each of `apiVersion`, `kind` and `spec`, with no blank line added between members.
decisions.reason: Entity.ts documents its members with multi-line blocks; adding blank lines would put non-comment lines in a diff that must be comment-only (NFR-2).

decisions.choice: Replace each three-line block with the full comment, keeping its `/**`, ` * @public` and ` */` lines, with tag order summary, `@remarks`, `@public`, `@param`, `@returns`.
rejected: a second comment block above the existing one
decisions.reason: API Extractor reads only the comment block nearest the declaration; ref.ts already orders `@public` before `@param` and `@returns`.

decisions.choice: Type guards in conditions.ts get `@returns`; validator methods and policy `enforce` methods state their result in the summary and remarks and get `@param` only.
decisions.reason: CommonValidatorFunctions documents its checks with `@param` only, and FR-2 alone asks for a stated return; fewer tags keep the comments short (NFR-1).

decisions.choice: Their comments do not mention throwing at all.
rejected: stating that they do not throw for a well-formed entity
decisions.reason: FR-4 allows either; leaving it out cannot be misread as an unqualified 'does not throw'.

decisions.choice: The comment names the package's `Entity` JSON schema, the one the code compiles (src/schema/Entity.schema.json), not the separate entity envelope schema.
rejected: calling it the entity envelope schema
decisions.reason: The package also exports an envelope validator built on EntityEnvelope.schema.json, which allows unknown root fields; the policy's schema does not, so the envelope name would mislead (NFR-1). The error message text still begins `Malformed envelope`.
The write contract allows only paths matching `.changeset/*catalog-model-tsdoc*.md`, and no file of that name exists.

units.behaviour: Fills the eight bare `/** @public */` comments of the `is<Kind>Entity` type guards with a summary, remarks, `@param` and `@returns`.
rules: 1. Every block keeps its existing `/**`, ` * @public` and ` */` lines untouched; text goes in only through the two insert sites per function: summary, a blank ` *` line, `@remarks`, a blank ` *` line, the remark and a blank ` *` line after the `/**` line; the `@param` and `@returns` lines after the ` * @public` line.

2. Per function, with K the kind name and T the interface: isApiEntity K=`API` T=ApiEntityV1alpha1; isComponentEntity K=`Component` T=ComponentEntityV1alpha1; isDomainEntity K=`Domain` T=DomainEntityV1alpha1; isGroupEntity K=`Group` T=GroupEntityV1alpha1; isLocationEntity K=`Location` T=LocationEntityV1alpha1; isResourceEntity K=`Resource` T=ResourceEntityV1alpha1; isSystemEntity K=`System` T=SystemEntityV1alpha1; isUserEntity K=`User` T=UserEntityV1alpha1.
3. Summary: Checks whether an entity is of the K kind.

4. Remark: The comparison of `kind` with K ignores case, so `K` in any letter case matches (write K once in the case shown and once in lower case as the example, e.g. `component` for Component). Only `kind` is checked: `apiVersion` and `spec` are not looked at, so a match does not mean that the entity conforms to {@link T}.
5. `@param entity - The entity to check`
6. `@returns True if the kind matches, narrowing the type of the entity to {@link T}`

7. Write the remark of rule 4 as plain sentences, for example for Component: The comparison of `kind` with `Component` ignores case, so `component` also matches. Only `kind` is checked: `apiVersion` and `spec` are not looked at, so a match does not mean that the entity conforms to {@link ComponentEntityV1alpha1}.

units.behaviour: Adds a TSDoc comment above each of the eight static validator methods of `KubernetesValidatorFunctions`, stating the rule it enforces.
rules: 1. Each comment: a one-sentence summary, then (where this list gives a remark) a blank ` *` line, `@remarks`, a blank ` *` line and the remark, then a blank ` *` line and `@param value - The value to check`. Indent 2 spaces. No `@returns`, no release tag, no `@see`.

2. Where a remark says DNS subdomain, write out this rule instead of a helper name: 1 to 253 characters, made of `.`-separated parts that are each 1 to 63 characters of lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit.

3. isValidApiVersion summary: Checks that the value is a valid entity `apiVersion`, such as `backstage.io/v1alpha1` or `v1`. Remark: The value must be a string that is either a version alone or a prefix and a version separated by a single `/`; a second `/` makes it invalid. The version is 1 to 63 ASCII letters and digits, with no other characters. The prefix, when present, must be a DNS subdomain (rule 2). Non-string values return `false`.

4. isValidKind summary: Checks that the value is a valid entity `kind`. Remark: The value must be a string of 1 to 63 characters that starts with an ASCII letter and contains only ASCII letters and digits. Non-string values return `false`.

5. isValidObjectName summary: Checks that the value is a valid entity name. Remark: The value must be a string of 1 to 63 characters that starts and ends with an ASCII letter or digit and contains only ASCII letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`; these separators can repeat, as in `a--b` or `a..b`. Non-string values return `false`.

6. isValidNamespace summary: Checks that the value is a valid entity namespace. Remark: The value must be a string of 1 to 63 characters made of lower-case ASCII letters, digits and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit; consecutive hyphens are allowed. Upper-case letters, `_` and `.` make it invalid. Non-string values return `false`.

7. isValidLabelKey summary: Checks that the value is a valid label key. Remark: The value must be a string that is either a name alone or a prefix and a name separated by a single `/`; a second `/` makes it invalid. The name follows the same rule as {@link KubernetesValidatorFunctions.isValidObjectName}, and the prefix, when present, must be a DNS subdomain (rule 2). Non-string values return `false`.

8. isValidLabelValue summary: Checks that the value is a valid label value. Remark: The empty string is valid; any other value must follow the same rule as {@link KubernetesValidatorFunctions.isValidObjectName}. Non-string values return `false`.

9. isValidAnnotationKey summary: Checks that the value is a valid annotation key. Remark: The rule is the same as for {@link KubernetesValidatorFunctions.isValidLabelKey}: a name alone or a prefix and a name separated by a single `/`, where the name follows the {@link KubernetesValidatorFunctions.isValidObjectName} rule and the prefix must be a DNS subdomain (rule 2). Non-string values return `false`.

10. isValidAnnotationValue summary: Checks that the value is a valid annotation value, which is any string, including the empty string. Remark: There is no length limit and no restriction on characters. Non-string values return `false`.

units.behaviour: Adds a TSDoc comment to `DefaultNamespaceEntityPolicy.enforce` stating when it returns the entity as is and when it returns a new object with the default namespace.
rules: 1. Summary: Fills in the policy's namespace when the entity's `metadata.namespace` is missing or `undefined`.

2. After a blank ` *` line, `@remarks` and a blank ` *` line, remark paragraph 1: When `metadata.namespace` is a non-empty string (the check is for any truthy value), the returned promise resolves to the same entity object, unchanged.

3. Remark paragraph 2 (after a blank ` *` line): Otherwise it resolves to a new object, never the entity that was passed in: the entity deep-merged over `{ metadata: { namespace } }`, where the namespace is the one given to the constructor, {@link DEFAULT_NAMESPACE} by default. The entity's own values win the merge unless they are `undefined`, so the namespace is filled in only when `metadata.namespace` is missing or `undefined`; an empty string or `null` is kept as it is. The entity that was passed in is not modified.
4. Then a blank ` *` line and `@param entity - The entity to apply the default namespace to`.
5. Never mention `undefined` as a result, never say the default is set for an empty namespace, and say nothing about throwing.
6. Indent the block 2 spaces; no `@returns`, no release tag.

rules: 1. Summary: Checks the format of the entity's envelope fields and resolves to the same entity, unchanged, when every checked field is valid.

After a blank ` *` line, `@remarks` and a blank ` *` line, remark paragraph 1: `apiVersion`, `kind` and `metadata.name` are required and checked with the `isValidApiVersion`, `isValidKind` and `isValidEntityName` functions of the {@link Validators} given to the constructor, which default to those of {@link makeValidator}. `metadata.namespace` is checked with `isValidNamespace` when it is not `undefined`. Every key and value of `metadata.labels` and `metadata.annotations` and every entry of `metadata.tags` are checked with the corresponding label, annotation and tag validators.

3. Remark paragraph 2 (after a blank ` *` line): For every entry of `metadata.links`, `url` is required and must be a valid URL, and `title` and `icon`, when not `undefined`, must be strings that are not empty or whitespace only. No other field, including `spec`, is checked.

4. Remark paragraph 3 (after a blank ` *` line): It throws an `Error` whose message names the field when a required field is `undefined` or `null`, when an optional field is `null`, when a validator throws, or when a field fails its validator.
5. Then a blank ` *` line and `@param entity - The entity to check`.
6. Never mention `undefined` as a result. Indent the block 2 spaces; no `@returns`, no release tag.
